name: Adam Rasner
bio: I am a Natural beekeeper and Soil regeneration student in the Soil Food Web Complete Practicum – Consultant Path

name: Alex Goemans
bio: A health-focused regenerative farm where soil, animals, and wildlife live in harmony. Through sustainable practices, our land provides for our family and beyond, while remaining a place of enjoyment, excellence, and learning. Guided by Soil Food Web principles and our work as a soil lab technician, we apply biology first—building structure, resilience, and nutrient-dense food. By opening the gate to others, we offer hands-on learning rooted in optimism for the future of whole-body health.

name: Alex Yakaumo
bio: Alex Yakaumo is a permaculture practitioner, agroforestry specialist, and soil biology consultant based in Suriname. As a consultant trained through the Soil Food Web School, he supports farmers, NGOs, and community projects in restoring soil health through biologically complete compost, compost extracts, and compost teas. His work combines practical field experience with microscopy-based soil analysis to help build resilient and regenerative farming systems.

name: Alinani
bio: Alinani Kawala is a Chemistry teacher at KCM Konkola Secondary Trust School in Zambia, with nearly five years of experience in science education. As a Soil Food Web Certified Laboratory Technician, he is passionate about applying soil biology to regenerative agriculture and sustainable land management. He is committed to bridging science and agriculture through education, soil health analysis, and practical solutions that promote healthy soils and resilient farming systems

name: Allen Skinner
bio: Allen has worked in the soil biology field since 2009. He authored a three-year NRCS Conservation Innovation Grant (CIG) that studied Dr. Elaine’s Soil Food Web School assessment and treatment methods for a 4-acre urban farm in Jacksonville, Florida. Allen consults with farmers, ranchers, urban gardeners, permaculture practitioners, as well as those in the landscape industry to transition them from a chemical- based nutrient program to a biological program. He delivers step-by-step guides on how to transition to soil biology-based plant growing, including biological composting programs.

name: Amanda Currie
bio: Farming on a Regnerative Farm with sheep, beef, vineyards and Clydesdales.

name: Amy Luck-MacGregor
bio: Amy came to Dr Elaine’s teachings after 15 years as a clinical speech-language pathologist. As an organic homesteader she struggled to grow food successfully until discovering the SFW approach. Many microscopic analyses, compost piles and workshops later, she has had a blast making relationships in her community and around the globe. Amy has a passion for proving the connection between soil biology and nutrient density and a knack for designing on-farm demonstration trials. If you are an early adopter, just curious, or simply get a sparkle in your eye when you think about soil, reach out!

name: Anja Fonseka
bio: Hi! My goal is to look at all the small details within the bigger picture, connect the dots and develop a practical plan. I give workshops in microscopy, composting and soil regeneration. I see my role as an accelerator for change: Improve soils not only at the biological level, but also in how we understand and work with natural systems. My training at the SFW School has equipped me with the tools to support this process, and I am excited to collaborate with people who share a passion for healthy, living soils, resilient food production, and strong microbial and human communities.

name: Anton de Jager
bio: I support regenerative farming at De Keur Estate, guided by working with nature and respect for creation. With 27 years of farming experience and six in regenerative agriculture, mentored by Todd Harrington, I focus on learning through measurement and adaptation. My work includes producing 3,000 m³ of BioComplete compost annually and having transitioned 155 hectares to regenerative practices.
area: Witzenberg Local Municipality, Western Cape, South Africa

name: Arjuna Aucone Cordaro
company: Muxirum Regeneração de Solos e Sistemas Vivos
bio: Muxirum is a consulting firm specializing in soil regeneration, biological management, and the design of living production systems, integrating soil science, microbiology, and regenerative practices.rnWe apply soil microbiological science to restore fertility, increase productivity, reduce input costs, and build more resilient agricultural systems.

name: Asha Sundararajan
bio: My interest in soil biology grew from years of gardening, composting, and exploring ecological approaches to soil and water health. Through NuBiomes, I work with growers, compost producers, gardeners, and land stewards to better understand the living biology in their soils and composts and turn that information into practical actions. By evaluating microbial communities, I help identify opportunities to improve nutrient cycling, support disease suppression, increase soil resilience, and guide amendment strategies that can be monitored and refined over time.

name: Astrid Harris
bio: After a long career in Police forensic work I have retrained in Organic Primary Production and Soil microbiology.rnI am a certified Lab Technician with Dr Elaine Ingham’s Soil Food Web School and able to carry out microbiology assessments of soil, compost and liquid amendments.rnI continue my training to become a qualified consultant

name: Aysen Ustunay
company: Hope For Soil - Toprakla Dost LTD.
bio: After a 25-year corporate career, she became an SFW consultant and mentor, guided by a lifelong passion for soil and living systems. Early health challenges that modern medicine could not resolve led her to restore her wellbeing through nutrient-dense food, igniting a search for the roots of true health. The teachings of Dr. Elaine Ingham revealed the missing link: SOIL MICROBES. She now consults on rebuilding soil biology in annual and perennial systems and finds deep fulfillment mentoring and collaborating with others who share a commitment to regenerating soil.

name: Barry McKenna
bio: I work in arboriculture within adult education and have a strong interest in soil science. I aim to share my enthusiasm for trees and the vital role soils play in their health. Arboriculture is often mistaken for tree cutting, but it is the science and practice of managing trees over their full lifespan. Soil–tree interactions govern vitality, resilience, and longevity. Trees are complex, long‑lived holobionts, not just timber, and informed arborists are essential to protect and sustain these living systems.

name: Bellbrae Garlic
bio: Soil, Compost and Extract Biological Assessments. Hand-grown organic garlic 🧄 Growing to regenerative farming & permaculture principles on a small scale family farm👩🏽‍🌾🧑‍🌾🐾 SXC cert. 25240

name: Ben Padwick
bio: Ben Padwick is a Director at WildSoils, working alongside his father, Nick Padwick, to deliver practical, large-scale biological solutions for land regeneration and to scale up the Soil Food Web approach. Ben focuses on biocomplete compost production, compost extracts, and innovative soil projects, including the use of human hair in soil testing. He leads baseline data collection, landscape recovery programmes, and long-term monitoring, helping farmers and land managers rebuild healthy, living soils with measurable results.
area: King\'s Lynn and West Norfolk, England, United Kingdom

name: Birgit Albertsmeier
bio: Birgit, a former trainer and programmer for a well-known office suite, began her Soil Food Web journey in 2014. She graduated from Dr. Elaine’s™ Soil Food Web School Consultant Training Program and holds a Permaculture Design Certificate. Birgit creates soil restoration plans using the Soil Food Web approach and advises on best implementation practices. She also teaches workshops on soil biology and microscopy. Based in the Netherlands, she works mainly in Dutch and German, sharing her passion for healthy soils.

name: Bonnie
bio: I received my bachelors degree in Ecology and see my study of the soil food web as an extension of my ecology education. A bio-complete soil food web maintains the healthy balance of an intact ecosystem. Reintroducing the soil food web and taking steps to maintain it mitigates the detrimental effects of broken nutrient cycles on a global scale, as well as creates the conditions for healthy, productive crops and pastures in our food systems. I hope to use my education to help growers in their journey of restoring soil health.

name: Brandi McCoy
bio: Brandi McCoy is a soil health coach, rancher, and Soil Food Web Lab Technician trained through the Soil Food Web School. A proud graduate of Integrity Soils\’ CREATE, she combines hands-on ranch experience with regenerative practices, guiding land stewards to see their operations as interconnected ecosystems. She helps clients interpret soil and land health, optimize grazing, and build resilient, profitable systems while prioritizing long-term ecosystem health.

name: Brenda Grate
bio: Brenda specializes in cultivating soil microorganisms to restore degraded soils for plant growth, nutrient cycling, structure, and water holding capacity. With 8 years of lab experience, including managing her own SFW lab, Brenda excels in soil health assessment, pathogen testing, PCR, and microscopy. Credentials: BS Biology & Soil Science (Humboldt State), Certified Soil Food Web Consultant (Elaine Ingham), Permaculture Design (UMass Amherst). Brenda is a bilingual US-Brazil dual citizen dedicated to sustainability, ecological restoration, reforestation, and planetary health.

name: Brian Daubenspeck
bio: Lab & Consultancy

name: Brian Vagg
bio: Brian was formerly in IT for 25 years before he made the switch to follow his passion. He completed Dr. Elaine’s™ Consultant Training Program in just 1 year and is now running a successful business as a Soil Food Web Consultant and Lab-Tech. When they are not working with clients throughout Northern California, Brian and his wife, Shelby, can be found raising biologically grown produce and animals on their homestead.

name: Brianna Dennison
bio: Growing up on her family\’s organic kiwifruit orchard in Te Puke developed a lifelong connection to the land and food production. Her hands-on experience spans over a decade in the kiwifruit and dairy farming industry, along with roles spent in market gardening, broad acre cropping, forestry wilding pine management, fruit sampling and soil lab testing, giving her a broad perspective on both conventional and regenerative systems. Brianna\’s focus is on supporting growers and farmers creating resilient and profitable farming systems centred on human, animal and soil health.
area: Te Puke, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand

name: Caroline Bustillos
bio: Certified Lab Technician currently working in the Los Angeles area in an urban farming setting. Parallelly working on a soil regeneration project in Bolivia.

name: Catheirne Mac Rae
bio: I have lived and worked with the soil in the southern tip of the Nicoya Peninsula of Costa Rica for the past 8 years. Prior to this I lived in the temperate Pacific Northwest of the United States. I am passionate about learning how soils, plants and environmental conditions function together to create healthy ecosystems. My strengths include relational observation skills in tropical ecosystems and analyzing soils

name: Charles Desmarais
bio: cash grain farmer in SW Ontario

name: Charlotte Huber
bio: At Humus & Co. Huber Industrie, we believe that the key to agricultural resilience lies in shifting the focus from synthetic inputs to living, dynamic soil biology. By restoring the natural soil food web, we help farmers decrease input costs, improve water retention, and grow truly nutrient-dense crops. rnrnUtilizing strict biological standards to manufacture high-quality, biologically diverse local compost and liquid amendments tailored to revive degraded soils.

name: Chase Jones
bio: Chase Jones is a permaculture designer, a soil ecologist, and a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) specialist based out of the southeastern United States. Chase’s focus involves using permaculture, in-depth site analysis, agroecology, soil ecology, and bioremediation to restore ecosystem function, often incorporating earthworks, polycultures, nutrient cycling systems, and strategies for helping communities manage their projects.

name: Christine Gust
bio: Christine Gust works with small-scale market farmers and gardeners across the Denver metro area, helping them build healthier, more diverse soil ecosystems. As a microbe ambassador, she brings the underground world to life through visits to schools and community organizations.rnTrained as a consultant and lab technician through Dr. Elaine Ingham’s Soil Food Web School, Christine also serves as a soil mentor with GoFarm & is a community partner of Cool Boulder. She holds a Permaculture Design Certificate, has several years of experience in plant nurseries, and is a member of Mile High Farmers.

name: Christine Lenches-HInkel
bio: Christine Lenches‑Hinkel, founder of 301 Organics, brings 25+ years of environmental expertise to leading soil restoration and bioremediation in Altadena, including recovery of Eaton Fire–impacted soils. A former URS environmental planner and the Rose Bowl Stadium\’s organics consultant, she applies microscopy and Soil Food Web principles to design biological treatments that rebuild soil structure, function, and post‑fire ecosystems.

name: Christopher Carlislle
bio: Certified 3 times since 2021 through soilfoodweb.com, Last Re-Cert was 2025. Re-Cert when it meets ROI expectation. I make continuous efforts to maintain my quality assurance. Been composting and growing plants naturely for 26yrs. Lived and worked on 30 organic farms; stayed on some for 2.5yrs. Worked independently on many regen projects: design/built: nutrient cycling chicken yards, large no-till market gardens, edible forest gardens… Currently building an edible forest garden in an urban setting (I\’m now rooted in New Port Richey, FL). Make and apply compost tea, extract, bio-simulates…
area: New Port Richey, FL, Florida, United States

name: Colleen Dempster
bio: Colleen Dempster is a certified Soil Food Web Laboratory Technician based in Ontario, Canada and founder of Rewild Soils. She specializes in microbial analysis of soils, composts, and liquid biological amendments. Over the past five years, she has analyzed hundreds of samples using microscopy and DNA profiling. Colleen enjoys working with large datasets to build baseline microbial data and identify meaningful patterns. She is working on Stage 3 of the Soil Food Web Consultant certification. nLet’s rewild soils together!

name: Dan Shazar
bio: My name is Dan, I am 44 years old, and I live in Israel. I grew up on a kibbutz, surrounded by land, trees, and agriculture, with both my father and grandfather managing fruit orchards. Over the years, this evolved into a deep personal connection to nature. In my twenties, I became increasingly aware of ecological issues and began exploring sustainable agriculture. Discovering the Soil Food Web approach was a turning point that brought together my experiences and inspired my ongoing path in soil biology.

name: Dani Vargas
bio: Dani is grateful to have been born at home with a midwife, in the ancestral homeland of the Payaya Nation (San Antonio, Tejas) and to have many mentors and wise people to guide them towards self-healing and wholeness. At age 9, they began working in agriculture on the family farm within the former territory of the Osage Nation in the foothills of the Ozark Mountains. Since the profound impact that rural living had on their youth, Dani has been on a life-long journey that revolves around what it means to live as a natural human being.

name: David Acuña
bio: Biologist and ecologist with background in conservation and livestock holistic management. Certified Soil Food Web Lab-Tech.
area: Villanueva de la Vera, Extremadura, Spain

name: Davis Limbach
bio: I am most interested in bringing people together in community. We become like the communities in the soil, serving all life by supporting each other. As a lab tech I am able to help us produce the best results in composting and application. rnMy small splash so far has extended beyond the home farm to other small farms and private homes, as well as our local eco tree service. I show people how to use the materials on their own land or from nearby to make awesome compost. Community compost is a whole-ecosystem approach that fosters diversity on every level through building relationships.

name: Debbie Naera
bio: I am a Soil Food Web lab Tech

name: Debbie Van Till
bio: Farmer, winemaker with a passion for working with Nature to increase biology in soil and plants to improve the 4 ecosystem processes in regenerative farming and gardening.

name: Derek Barbe
bio: Regenerative Soil Consultant-in-Training, specializing in biologically active compost, and soil microscopy.

name: Dominique Laínez
bio: Dominique, agronomist with a deep commitment to soil biological regeneration and the transition toward living, self-sustaining systems in both agricultural and urban environments.rnShe works as an independent consultant, leading soil restoration processes using Biologically Complete Inoculants, transforming organic waste into high-quality biological amendments, and adapting equipment for effective field application. Her work spans from perennial and annual crop systems to urban green infrastructure, aligning with strategies for water infiltration, urban resilience, and heat island mitigation.

name: Dora Tkalec
bio: A teacher by training and gardener at heart, Dora Tkalec discovered permaculture in 2012 — a turning point that led her deep into the science and magic of compost, and to recognizing soil as the foundation of all functioning ecosystems. She has been practicing the Soil Food Web approach since 2020. Working with farmers, growers, and landscape professionals, she restores soil health through bioactive composting tailored to each farm’s own resources. She believes that understanding natural complexity and genuine human cooperation can lead us to the better world our hearts know is possible.

name: Doug Ayers
bio: Completed the Foundation courses. Got certified as a Microscope Lab Technician. Passed the Liquids Class. Will start on the Final Project soon.

name: Dr Carla Portugal
bio: Director of Science at Soil Domains and Soil Food Web School. Ph.D. graduate from Oregon State University, my background spans biology, environmental sciences & engineering, and sustainable forest management. At Soil Domains, I lead soil food web consultancy globally and microorganism-based product development in Brazil. At SFWS, I mentor students in soil biology analysis, composting, and soil health, while bridging the gap for Portuguese-speaking communities. Having worked on UNESCO projects, I unite engineering and biology to restore water cycles and regenerate ecosystems.

name: Duncan Pepper
bio: Ecologist, fungi and soil geek

name: Elias Bajalia
bio: Elias Bajalia is a well-rounded steward of the land. He is a graduate of Dr. Elaine’s™ Soil Food Web School Consultant Training Program and is a certified Permaculture Designer as well. He has been focusing on growing organic food for 20 years. He integrates a whole systems approach to agriculture, which starts from the life in the soil, or more often than not, a lack thereof. Visit his Biotilth website to find out how he can help you turn your dirt back into healthy, living soil.

name: Elizabeth Romo-Rabago
bio: Elizabeth is a biologist with a Master’s in Sustainable Energy Development whose early connection to land began on her family’s farm and garden. She later expanded her expertise through advanced training in soil biology, permaculture, ecosystem restoration, and extensive coursework with Dr. Elaine’s Soil Food Web School including certification as a Lab Technician. With 20+ years of experience, she supports growers and communities through microbial assessments and regenerative training, earning multiple awards for her commitment to community led ecological regeneration.

name: Eric Feiler
bio: After retiring from academia in the early 2000\’s, Eric moved to remote Southern Utah where he took a job as caretaker of a 200-acre property. In 2016 Eric took a week-long workshop with Dr. Ingham. Eric was immediately a convert, and continued his education under Dr. Ingham through the Soil Food Web School. In 2019 Eric was hired by the Soil Food Web School as a Consultant Training Program Mentor/Instructor. In 2022 he was certified as a Soil Food Web Consultant. He currently is owner and director of High Desert Soil Works, LLC, a soil fertility company working throughout southern Utah.

name: Eric Johnson
bio: Collector of Malus sieversii and other wild apples. Native plants, soil health, renewable energy & nature-based solutions, climate issues, cover crops.

name: Fahri Ulucay
bio: An engineer by background, Fahri Ulucay transitioned into soil microscopy out of a fascination with the Soil Food Web. He enjoys bridging the gap between systems thinking and soil microbiology to understand the living networks within soil and compost, and how they relate to plant health and the nutritional density of food. Passionate about making soil science approachable and down-to-earth, Fahri looks forward to collaborating with UK allotment owners, market gardens, and community projects, helping local growers look beneath the surface to better understand their soil’s natural biology.

name: Faith Moeser
bio: Faith Moeser runs Soil Dynamix out of Spokane, Washington. After starting a garlic farm, Faith faced the same challenges many farmers encounter—declining soil health and inconsistent yields. That journey led her to the Soil Food Web School, where she saw firsthand the transformative power of soil biology. Through Soil Dynamix, Faith combines biological principles with mineral balancing to help farmers and gardeners build healthy soils and grow productive, resilient crops.

name: Fatma Kamai
bio: I am a soil researcher at the Agricultural Research Center in Libya, and the Soil Food Web School foundation courses bridged a critical academic gap. Prevailing conventional practices—reliant on chemical inputs and intensive tillage—disrupt the soil microbiome, ignoring its vital role in nutrient cycling, disease suppression, and weed management. Witnessing this degradation drove my passion to work with nature. Inspired by Dr. Elaine Ingham, I am training to become a soil food web consultant.
area: Al bayda, Jabal al Akhdar, Libya

name: FELIPE LUPUSELLA
bio: Agri Livre is an initiative dedicated to bringing soil back to life through regenerative agriculture. We provide Soil Food Web biological analyses and practices that restore ecosystems, strengthen natural fertility, and support farmer autonomy. Our mission is to build living, resilient agricultural systems aligned with nature’s processes.

name: Fernando Gutiérrez
bio: I am a Soil Food Web Certified Laboratory Technician (CLP), working with farmers and ecosystem restoration projects to develop biologically functional vermicompost, extracts and compost teas.rnrnMy work focuses on applying soil microbiology to practical systems, including compost and vermicompost production, biological amendments, and nature-based solutions such as wastewater treatment using vermifilters. I support projects from analysis and validation to real-world implementation, with an emphasis on measurable biological performance.

name: Filip Golebiewski
bio: Farmer, soil enthusiast, architect, machine builder, inventor.

name: Gael Mion
bio: Certified lab technician for soil food web analyses!

name: Holly Headrick
bio: Certified as a current soil lab-tech through the Soil Food Web and currently taking the consulting course.

name: Ilona Angelova
bio: As the founder of Underground Labs, my work brings together biological microscopy, composting, and soil health advocacy — all aimed at spreading knowledge, supporting resilient ecosystems.rn Within our Soil Food Web Bulgaria community, we aim to make the SFW methodology work in agricultural realities. My passions also include stewardship for compost quality standards, policy development, and support for regenerative agriculture.

name: Ireth Garcia
bio: The complexity of the living world fascinates me. After working as a scientific researcher in Biophysics for 7 years, I am addressing my passion for healthy soils and just societies through a varied training curriculum, including the SFWS CTP. This has given me a holistic view of the various layers of our food systems. You can contact me for: – SFW biological assessments – On/offline lectures on composting, soil life, and regenerative practices- Hands-on and team-building workshops around soil. I am also facilitator for the Living Soils Workshop. I speak English, Nederlands, y Español.

name: Isadora Schmidt
bio: I offer soil lab work (soil food web assessments, SAP, chemical etc), biologically active and tailor made amendments (solid and liquid), support with transition strategies and improving systems, and research projects. I’ve worked with agroforestry systems, permaculture design and regenerative agriculture.

name: Jacopo Orazi
bio: Radice Soil Solutions is a soil health consultancy based in Tairāwhiti, working with growers, landowners, and restoration projects to improve soil function and long-term system resilience. Our work combines soil biology testing, including eDNA and microscopy, with practical field insights to translate complex data into clear, actionable decisions. The focus is on helping clients better understand their soil as a living system, reduce reliance on inputs, and build more resilient and productive land.

name: Jamie Dickinson
bio: Jamie holds an MS in International Agricultural Development from UC Davis and a certificate in organic gardening from the Farm and Garden Project in Santa Cruz, CA. As Assistant Director of the US Peace Corps in Panama, he designed and led a hillside farming extension project for subsistence farmers. Later, he served on the board of Sustainable Harvest International and studied herbal medicine. He’s interested in compost, extract and tea production as well as applying biological principles to restoring disturbed land and supporting thriving farms, gardens and productive landscapes.

name: Janét Moore
bio: Hello biophilic friends! I moved to Rapid City, SD in 2023 and am very happily a staff member of the SD Soil Health Coalition! I majored in Soil Science, but was disappointed soil microbes were largely ignored. After graduating (USU 2006), I worked for the NRCS mapping soils in remote locations of WY and N. MN, and developed a deep appreciation for native prairie. Then for many years I was in coatal OR working as a co-op produce manager while community organizing on forestry reform issues, on a Biointensive farm, and more recently in grassland management with bison and cattle ranchers.
area: Rapid City, South Dakota, United States

name: Jason Gearheart
bio: Jason started his company, Integrated Elements Compost, while finishing his consultancy, to provide high quality biologically active compost and worm compost at volume. His passion is to revolutionize soil health and bridge the gaps between organic diversions, making high quality compost and application methods. Jason is an FAA certified drone pilot and plans to research this technology to support the process of innovation in building soil health.

name: Jean-Baptiste Nazarie
bio: Ingénieur en agriculture spécialisé dans la production et le commerce des céréales. J\’explore par curiosité les techniques de l\’agriculture régénératrices pour répondre aux enjeux économiques, écologiques et sanitaires de la production agricole. Je suis un technicien de laboratoire certifié depuis 2022.

name: Jennifer Neufeld
bio: With a BSc in Environmental Studies, a Graduate Certificate in Sustainable Community Development, and a Permaculture Design Certificate, Jennifer combines scientific knowledge with practical experience in soil health assessment, microscopy, regenerative agriculture, and ecological land management. Jennifer works with landowners, gardeners, schools, and communities to interpret soil biology and build resilient, living soils that support healthy plants and thriving ecosystems. Her passion is environmental education. Check her out on Linked In.

name: Jenny Sanderson
bio: My composting and soil health journey has led me to working full time as Allotments Officer for the Local Council, here in NW England. I volunteer for Garden Organic UK, promoting home composting – and larger scale too when the opportunity arises – showing what makes good compost special (the soil microbes, of course!) I am happy to arrange a chat about composting methods. I can provide the standard Soil Food Web microscope analysis, by arrangement, for small numbers of samples. For something less formal and definitely more fun, you can join me for a live look at the life in your sample.

name: Jeroen Boss
bio: Based in the western Algarve, Portugal, I am an agricultural consultant, land steward and ecological restoration practitioner working across projects in Portugal and the Netherlands since 2016. My practice is grounded in the three pillars of ecosystem restoration — water, soil, and vegetation. The SFW training deepened my understanding of compost quality, microbial analysis, and biological soil amendments. I apply these principles alongside syntropic agroforestry and water retention earthworks, drawing on a strong foundation in farming contexts gained through my work in The Netherlands.

name: Jerry Field
bio: A raspberry farmer who has years of trying different techniques, have been studying the soil food web for two years, certified as a lab tech in 2025. Invloved in teaching subsitance farming in Africa, mainly Zambia for 20 years.

name: Jesper Andersson
bio: Hi ,my name is Jesper ,I am an organic meat producer located outside Falköping ,Västra Götaland I am interested in biological composting and assessing biology in soil and compost using a microscope.

name: Joaquin Perez
bio: Soil Food Web trained microscopist and Biotechnology student based in Argentina. Co-founder of Tasty Living Soils, where I work with biologically complete compost, living soil systems, soil amendments, and grower education. My experience combines microscopy, compost quality assessment, soil biology analysis, and practical implementation of regenerative growing practices. I help growers understand their soil biology, identify limitations, and improve nutrient cycling, plant health, resilience, and productivity through biology-based management.

name: Joe Zanotelli
bio: 25 years as an electrical engineer taught Joe to find root causes, not patch symptoms. That same discipline brought him to soil. After two years running Compost Teana’s and watching chemically-dependent gardens come back to life with living biology, he founded SoCal BioAmendments. Certified by Dr. Elaine Ingham’s Soil Food Web School and trained under Gabe Brown and Ray Archuleta at the Soil Health Academy, every batch he delivers is verified under the microscope.

name: josefina bergsten
bio: Soil Food Web Consultant and market garden grower based in southern Sweden, with over ten years of hands-on experience growing diverse vegetables on permanent beds. Learning directly from Dr. Elaine Ingham through the Soil Food Web School transformed the way I grow, by focusing on microbe-rich compost and living soils. When I’m not out in the field, I love spending time at the microscope, exploring the tiny life forms that make healthy soils possible. I enjoy sharing what I’ve learned with growers, farmers, and land managers in the region.

name: Joshua Weybright
bio: Josh Weybright is a Soil Food Web consultant and educator based in New Mexico. Through Bright Way Ag., he helps farmers, ranchers, and gardeners restore soil health using compost, extracts, mineral balancing, and microscopy. Josh empowers land stewards to build resilient soils that improve plant nutrition, reduce inputs, and strengthen natural systems. He also teaches classes on soil biology and co-founded the Growing Soil Health Collective, supporting communities in creating thriving, self-sustaining ecosystems.
area: Santa Fe, New Mexico, United States

name: José Santa Cruz
bio: José Santa Cruz is a Certified Soil Food Web Lab-Tech (CLT) with professional training as an agronomist and an M.Sc. in Agricultural Economics (Fulbright, USA). Since 2016, his work has focused on soil health and sustainable production systems, using microscopy-based soil biology analysis to support regenerative agriculture and sustainable food production.

name: Judith Green
bio: German, beekeeper (teacher), permaculturist, SFW Lab tech, farmer, wife to an Englishman, mother of two young adults, living in France since 25 years, regenerating a rundown dairy farm
area: Saint-Georges-sur-Erve, Pays de la Loire, France

name: Julia Dupuis
bio: My background is a BSc (Chem) and an MSc (Environment and Management). Being a Certified Lab Practitioner allows me to pull everything I\’ve learned about soil, chemistry and the environment together to better understand different soil profiles and needs. I help my clients understand the issues with their soil and how to improve it leading to better yields, less pests and disease, increased water holding capacity add more. The answer is in the soil – let\’s find it.

name: Julian Ravenscroft
bio: Julian knows what it’s like to think growing plants in soil is cursed. But it was his own journey of seeing plants become naturally disease and pest resistant through investing in soil biology that led him to start his own consultant business. He has experience helping farms, orchards, gardens, and contaminated soils in need of mitigation. He loves to use his mathematics education background to find empowering, profitable solutions for his clients. Julian believes working with soil and growing plants should bring JOY instead of non-stop COSTLY and STRESSFUL decisions.

name: Julie Shedko
bio: Julies soil journey started by completing a Permaculture Design and Permaculture Teachers Training Course in 2009. She was hired to design a private two- acre farm which later became Lettuce Grow Farms and Educational Center located in El Prado, New Mexico in 2010. Struggling as a grower with poor soil structure she enrolled to study at the Soil Food Web School in 2020 and has completed the Foundation Courses, Laboratory Technician Program and the Consultant Training Program. Currently, Julie is a Certified Consultant and operates a composting business.

name: Justin Whittaker
bio: Justin Whittaker is a citizen scientist, farmer, and mycophile focused on understanding the biology of boreal soils. He is the founder of Arctic Roots Analytics, a biological soil lab in Interior Alaska specializing in microscopic analysis of soil, compost, and compost extracts. Drawing on his experience managing two Interior Alaska farms, he helps farmers and gardeners better understand their soil food web and gain practical insights for building resilient, biologically active soils.

name: Kathy SCHREIBER
company: 1% FOR YOUR KIDS Climate Action Program
bio: GOOD NEWS! I can show you how to gain the 6 Soil Superpowers: increased yields, improved nutrient density, suppress weeds, pests and diseases, lessen run off & sequester carbon! Whether you have a farm, a city lot, or a garden bed, real change is possible. In addition to consulting 1% For Your Kids Climate Action Program, people like you become Climate Heroes. Successes: 18.5 tons of CO₂/suburban orchard, 1.74%+ soil carbon/urban yard, & 3.5%+ soil carbon during a six-month green bean trial. The way Mother Nature intended. Contact us today to put the 6 Soil Superpowers to work for you

name: Keisha Wheeler
bio: I wear many hats, with a primary focus on building community around microbe farming. Im passionate about revealing unseen life in soil through microscope images and videos. Explore my work at MyMicrobes.org or follow @SoilMicrobeLibrary and @catalyst_microbe_adventure on Instagram and Facebook. I consult with Catalyst BioLogical Solutions, providing on-site services to build and maintain soil fertility. As a founding member of the Sierra Soil Biology Association, I collaborate with consultants, lab techs, and advocates to regenerate soil and enhance food quality by increasing microbial biomass

name: Kent Holle
bio: Kent Holle is a Certified Soil Consultant and Lab Technician through the Soil Food Web School, with over 35 years in the turf and land management industry. Based in Colorado, he has worked alongside the EPA and Colorado State University to reduce synthetic inputs and implement biology-first systems across school districts and landscapes. Through ByDesign Soil, Kent helps farmers, ranchers, and land managers rebuild soil function using microscopy, bio-complete compost, and practical transition strategies that restore resilience, productivity, and stewardship of the land.

name: Kevin Fretz
bio: Kevin Fretz is a lifelong ecological entrepreneur. In 2016 Kevin Fretz founded Green Earthology after more than 30 years working with recycling, soil restoration, and landscaping companies worldwide. Kevin’s company uses Dr. Elaine’s Soil Foodweb principles on their projects across the U.S.

name: Kevin Krause
bio: Kevin was an Iowa farm kid, attended the U.S. Air Force Academy, and completed a 26-year military career. After seeing “Food Inc,” in 2008, Kevin and his wife began critically researching nutrition, links to health, and flaws of Industrial Ag. They started their own farm in 2015 raising beef, pork, chicken, eggs, and honey bees. The quest for better pasture and “nutrient dense” food led Kevin to training with Korean Natural Farming, the Soil Food Web, and Permaculture. He helps others leverage biology over chemistry to enhance their soils, their crops, and their portion of the planet.

name: Krisi Olivero
bio: Krisi lives for soil microbes, bad jokes and helping others grow. Living in Chattanooga, TN she works with clients in the Southeast US, testing, consulting and teaching. Alter Eco Farms also produces small batch biologically complete compost and extracts, along with other soil amendment products such as protozoa infusions, humic acid and inoculated biochar. At Alter Eco Farms we want everyone to experience the magic of growing in healthy soil, and we\’re here to help you achieve that, no matter where you are starting from. We currently specialize in home gardens, lawns and farms under 5 acres.

name: Kyle Babcock
bio: Kyle developed a deep love for nature while growing up in the ski town of Steamboat Springs, Colorado—skiing in the Rocky Mountains and gardening with his grandparents in Paonia. These early experiences sparked a lifelong curiosity about how plants grow. After earning a Horticulture degree and an Advanced Permaculture Design Certificationrnfrom Oregon State University, Kyle still had a question to answer. This search led him to Dr. Elaine Ingham and the world of soil microbiology. Now, as a Soil Food Web Consultant, Kyle helps farmers and gardeners restore soil health utilizing biology.

name: Kylie Pickles
bio: I am interested in regenerative agriculture practices and am putting my learnings of the SFW into practice on our shedding sheep property in SW Victoria, Australia. I look forward to sharing our results with others interested in regenerating their soils.

name: Laura Barnwell
bio: Having been a geologist for over 30 years, I currently teach classes in sustainability and climate risk, with the emphasis on biological diversity and ecosystem resilience. This was the perfect background for me to dive into soil health, because it’s an extension of what I love- people and the earth! As a Certified Soil Food Web Lab-Tech (CLT), I specialize in providing biological analysis of soil and compost, providing microbial identification succession assessments. Healthy soil means healthy people and a healthier tomorrow!
area: East Amwell Township, New Jersey, United States

name: Leif Busk
bio: Leif is a Farmer, Crop adviser, and Agro-engineer, and holds Permaculture Design Certificates in permaculture and regenerative design. He has been teaching compost making, permaculture, regenerative farming, and gardening in Denmark and Africa since 1985, and focuses on using regenerative and holistic methods.rnLeif strives to support nature’s biological cycle of SOIL-PLANTS-ANIMALS and to make farming and food production a regenerative copy of nature, emphasizing reduced input and increased outputs. He has found that using a microscope to identify and quantify the Soil Food Web is beneficial.

name: Leisha, Living Ground,
bio: Leisha Giddings is a certified SFW Consultant and educator based in Ecuador. She founded Living Ground Project, a working education and demonstration project centered on soil to plate systems, preservation, and ecological literacy. Through compost, gardens, microbial observation, food processing, and traditional preservation, the project focuses on witnessing soil recovery and translating living soil biology into resilient, self reliant food systems rooted in place. The aim is to restore soils, empower people and become a living destination to witness and learn.

name: Leon du Plessis
company: PINC Permaculture Institute of the Northern Cape
bio: I have a background in alternative medicine with a Masters degree. I co-run a permaculture demonstration site and market garden called PINC (Permaculture Institute of the Northern Cape). We offer short courses to the local community on topics like permaculture, soil health, composting, and self-sufficiency. My hands-on work includes making thermophilic compost following the school’s guidelines and managing a well-established vermicomposting system. As a trained Soil Food Web lab technician, I analyse soil, compost, and biological extracts for our site, community members, and local farmers.
area: Renosterberg Local Municipality, Northern Cape, South Africa

name: Leslie Lewis
bio: Leslie W. Lewis, Ph.D., had a first career as a college professor and executive. She approaches the study of soil health as a researcher and writer as well as an organic grower with decades of experience as a vegetable farmer. She now puts her business experience and hands-on growing knowledge together with her passion for knowledge and living systems thinking. She offers farmers, homesteaders, and residential householders consulting services that are conceptual, practical, and appropriate to scale. She also offers seminars and workshops for organizations and groups.

name: Lina Alegre
bio: Lina Alegre is a Soil Food Web Certified Lab Technician based in northern New Mexico, where she runs Reverdecer.org — a consulting practice dedicated to soil, water, and microbiome health. She serves communities across northern New Mexico through hands-on analysis, education, and outreach, including work with the NM Soil Health Working Group. Lina also coordinates continuing education and community programs at Northern New Mexico College, weaving regenerative soil science into institutional and community learning. She is a co-conspirator in building healthier land and thriving ecosystems.

name: Lisa Price
bio: A passionate educator on soil life and its inner workings. Lisa offers a soil analysis service of microbial life in your soil, compost or potting mix and can consult on farm or home gardens. Often found with her hands in the earth, Lisa is right at home in Ravenshoe on a biodynamic beef and vegetable farm that she runs with her partner Simon. They sell seedlings to the home gardeners and support and empower people to grow their own food.

name: Lori von der Heydt
bio: I am a naturopathic doctor informed by my first love, biology and my education in ecology. Nature heals. From the soil up.

name: Maggie judd
bio: I come from a military and electronics background but have always longed to have a life working outside and closer with nature. After the Army, I moved to Colorado, USA and researched Permaculture, Agroforestry, and Homesteading, which led me to Dr. Elaine\’s Soil Food Web School. Since getting my Microscopy Certification, I have decided to go forward with Consultant Training and helping others fix their soil the way my property so desperately needs it as well. Be happy and play in the dirt!

name: Marcelino Meincke
bio: Farmer and regenerative agriculture entrepreneur working at the intersection of soil science, plant nutrition, and practical field application. I develop biologically driven fertility systems that strengthen soil, crops, and livestock while reducing dependence on external inputs. By integrating engineering, data analysis, and hands-on experimentation, I translate soil insights into real-world results—building resilient systems and producing nutrient-dense food profitably.
area: Estrela, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

name: Maria Loper
bio: Maria Loper is a soil health consultant specializing in soil biology, compost systems, regenerative agriculture, and ecological restoration. She graduated from the SFW School and Certified SFW Technician program in 2021. Maria works with farmers, ranchers, gardeners, and landowners to improve soil function through biological assessments, compost production, pasture restoration, mineral balancing and water retention landscape design. She is focused on creating practical, repeatable systems that help clients build confidence and long-term success in regenerative land management.

name: Mario Villamiel
bio: Mario is a regenerative agriculture and soil health consultant specializing in Mediterranean ecosystems. His work combines the Soil Food Web approach with a holistic, systems perspective that views soil, plants, water, and management as interconnected.rnrnWith experience in organic farming, composting systems, bioferments, and agroecological design, Mario supports farmers in restoring degraded soils and building resilient production systems. His focus is on site-specific strategies that improve soil biology, ecosystem function, and long-term farm sustainability.

name: Marissa Busch
bio: Marissa Busch and her husband, Duane, farm 1,000 acres of non-GMO corn, barley, oats, and hay near Milaca, MN, while raising seven children and multiple livestock species. Their no-till operation uses living cover crops, aerobic compost, and biological inputs instead of synthetic fertilizers. Through on-farm testing and microscopy, Marissa monitors soil biology, restores microbial life, and improves plant and animal health. They are transitioning to organic, going beyond certification to regenerate their soils.
area: South Fork Township, Minnesota, United States

name: Matthew Kling
bio: My professional experience in agriculture is primarily in vineyards and winemaking. I was co-owner of La Gramiere from 2005 – 2015. My current company, Solvif, is a soil and environment regeneration company currently focused on building zero-plastic compost tea brewers that provide the highest level of mixing and aeration of any brewer on the market. Brewers from 250L to 5000L. Installations in the Netherlands, Spain, France and Austria.

name: Megan Weeber
bio: A lifelong obsession with the world eventually lead Megan into the Regenerative Agriculture movement. For just shy of a decade, she has been pouring over every book, podcast and course related to the subject. A city girl, returning to her roots in Yakima, Washington. She was strongly influenced by her grandparents hailing from farms and ranches in Ellensburg, Naches Heights and Ephrata. It’s important for Megan to make an impact in her community, where her family has spent several generations working and calling the Eastside home.

name: Melissa Rodgers
bio: A life pivot took me on quite the journey, and ultimately lead me to Dr Elaine\’s Soil Food Web School. I am so grateful!! I have discovered my passion for advocating for soil health, food waste reduction and all things composting (especially vermicomposting!!). I am enthusiastically working to build community through connection, workshops and events, and welcome the opportunity to collaborate and learn more about your goals.

name: Michael Evrard
bio: For agriculture systems, city-development, parklands & gardening communities I offer guidance within soil-related projects; also drawn to projects on nutrient-dense foods; focus on microbiology in soils and also in compost & compost related products; offer services in german and english

name: Michael Frey
bio: My deep fascination with nature and its complex systems led me from permaculture to the Soil Food Web. At Soily, we focus on regenerating life in the soil—and with it, the soil itself—quickly, effectively, and at scale. I believe this is the most powerful lever to restore local cycles and transform our food systems from the ground up.

name: Michel Koma Boré
bio: My name is Michel Koma Boré, and I am from Guinea. I work at the Shalam Agropastoral Center in Macenta, where I support rural communities through agriculture and livestock development. My role is to help farmers become financially self-reliant by providing training, technical guidance, and promoting sustainable farming practices. I am passionate about rural development, agricultural innovation, and empowering communities to improve their livelihoods.

name: Miguel Ventura ¦ PermaBioLogic
bio: INTEGRATED CONSULTANCY ¦ PERMACULTURE, SOIL BIOLOGY AND CIVIL ENGINEERING

name: Mike Blancke
bio: Mike has spent his career in turf and around farming. Being convinced there must be a better way than conventional agriculture, he found the Soil Food Web. As a Certified Lab Tech, he can identify and measure which soil microorganisms are present and which may be lacking to help people reach their soil health and plant goals.

name: Murat Akhuy
bio: Murat, having started the Türkiye Permaculture Research Institute together with a few friends, focused more on the soil regeneration aspects of permaculture and attended a seminar named as “Art of Microbiology Herding” in 2016 where he was exposed to the ideas of Elaine Ingham. As the issues related to the degradation of farming soil in Türkiye grew each year due to the excessive use of synthetic inputs and tilling, he decided to take part in SFW’s CTP program and has actively been involved in giving educational seminars and providing consultancy service for growers of all sizes since then.

name: Nate Christenson
bio: I\’m a certified lab tech in central Iowa, who is passionate about restoring life from soil to soul! We live on a diversified produce and grain farm, and are actively experimenting with biology based, regenerative and holistic practices to restore a healthy, vibrant functioning soil and farm ecosystem. Knowing what microbes are in your soil and compost amendments is the foundation to restoring a healthy living soil!

name: Nathalie Sequeira
bio: In her work as a landscape gardener, Nathalie has been gathering experience for many years in applying the principles of permaculture and the Soil Food Web to the customized implementation of nature-based techniques for the ecological regeneration of urban landscapes. rnShe is focused on working with the cycles of nature and its rhythms to shift those spaces towards resilience with high ecosystem-services impact, promoting all-round health that starts with the soil and includes all creatures. rnHer consultations focus on supporting you to transition to this future-proof approach.

name: Nauras
bio: Nauras IndorirnPermaculture Practitioner & Facilitator | Regenerative Agriculturist rnNauras Indori is a passionate permaculture practitioner and facilitator, with a deep commitment to regenerative agriculture and soil health. Their expertise lies in designing land systems that work in harmony with nature, ensuring that both ecosystems and communities thrive. Nauras has collaborated with the Meghalaya Basin Development Management Agency in the Garo Hills, focusing on soil and water conservation efforts in this ecologically sensitive region.

name: Nicholas Garcia
bio: Nicholas García KnightrnBritish-Mexican soil health consultant and researcher based in Xalapa, Mexico. M.Sc. in Tropical Agroecosystems; PhD candidate at INECOL studying compost microbiology and biological suppression of Fusarium oxysporum and Globodera rostochiensis. Certified Soil Food Web Lab Technician (CTP Stage 2). Founder of Mecate, a soil health consultancy serving producers transitioning to regenerative systems across Latin America. Works in English, Spanish, and Portuguese.rnContact: [email protected] | +52 228 109 1155

name: Nicholas Matteis
bio: The microbiological world is a wonder to me. To witness its complexity and diversity in order to understand how it manifests in the greater complexity of an ecosystem is what most captures my interest. I aim to contribute to the diversity of microorganisms that create a healthy soil food web. If I may be of any service to that end by way of my recent certification as a Soil Food Web lab technician please do contact me – I would love to help!

name: Nicola Peill-Moelter
bio: I am lifelong environmentalist with a passion for Nature-based solutions. After receiving my PhD in environmental engineering science from Caltech in 1997 I led corporate sustainability at Akamai Technologies and VMware, implementing renewable energy and product-efficiency innovation. In 2018, I read Dirt to Soil about regenerative farming principles and was hooked, an economic and scalable way to address the environmental and economic challenges of this industry. As a Soil Food Web consultant I collaborate with the farming community to adopt biological practices for better outcomes.

name: Niels de Jong
bio: MicroVida TV founders Niels and Priya specialize in soil regeneration through microorganisms, permaculture, and syntropic farming. Their journey began in the Canary Islands, where reviving their garden deepened their link between soil and human health. Now in Ecuador, they guide others via workshops, soil analysis, and consultancy. By fostering local collaboration, they nurture the planet’s vital resource: healthy soil. Their mission builds ecological resilience and sustainable practices, ensuring a thriving future for all life

name: Noah Neva
bio: Hello! My name is Noah and I am a Soil Food Web Laboratory Technician dedicated to helping my community better understand the biology that drives healthy, resilient soils. My work focuses on the beneficial microorganisms that play essential roles in nutrient cycling, plant health, and ecosystem function. Please don\’t hesitate to reach out to me, I love talking about soil and preaching sustainable practices!

name: Norm Hansen
bio: I am a soil focused lab technician with three years of hands-on experience with the Soil Food Web. As a SFW Lab Technician, we use a microscope to primarily test samples of soil and compost looking for essential beneficial microbiology and physical characteristics typical in healthy soil. Additionally, we utilize regenerative soil practices with our own organic vegetable production. I am currently training to become a Soil Food Web Consultant. We are passionate about improving soil quality to grow healthy, nutrient-dense food and helping farmers and gardeners build resilient, living soils.

name: Norman Higgins
bio: I am passionate about soil, compost, soil microbes and ecosystems. I have more than 3 decades of farming experience. I love the challenge of transforming poorly performing soils and plants into productive ecosystems with the right balance of minerals and microbes.
area: Tauranga, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand

name: Pascal Kubota
bio: Wheat breeder with focus on microbiome and plant health

name: Pasquale Caccavella
bio: After a decade as a packaging engineer, Pasquale answered a deeper calling: to heal the soil that feeds us. A lifelong mycologist with hands-on experience in regenerative hemp cultivation in partnership with Honeybee Hemp Farms, Pasquale founded Salem Soil Solutions in Winston-Salem, North Carolina. He crafts biologically dense compost and premium vermicompost in-house while offering microscopy assessments, soil testing reports, and personalized consulting. He partners with farmers, gardeners, and landowners to enhance their understanding of soil biology, applications, and system improvements

name: Pati Jiménez
bio: I am an ecologist and soil microbiology practitioner passionate about ecosystem health and regenerative pastoralism. Trained in climate science and certified in the Soil Food Web approach, I focus on restoring soil microbial life as the foundation of resilient landscapes. I believe well-managed herbivores are key allies in regenerating biodiversity, rebuilding carbon-rich soils, and adapting our food systems to climate and global change.

name: Peter Hanes
bio: Semi Retired Professional Pilot with a passion for Soil, Sun, Sea, Surf, Food, Wine and People. Invested soil steward, Gardener and green living practioner.
area: Cape Town, Western Cpe, South Africa

name: Pierre Joseph
bio: I am a raw earth builder, gardener, and soil ecologist, passionate about ecosystem restoration and food cultivation, particularly orchards. Since 2022, I have had the privilege of caring for a beautiful 2.7-hectare property in Marvão, Central Portugal. I am committed to soil regeneration and supporting my community by offering training, soil analysis, and guidance for the transition to regenerative agroforestry.

name: Predrag Paunovic
bio: I am Predrag Paunovic from Lazarevac, Serbia. With a background in acting and environmental stewardship, I hold a Master’s in Environmental Protection in Agriculture and am a certified permaculture designer trained in Vedic agriculture. As a member of Permaculture Serbia and Blagodat Serbia, I have practiced regenerative farming on my land for a decade, guided by Dr. Elaine Ingham’s Soil Food Web approach. I share my experience through workshops and outreach, inspiring farmers to trust nature’s processes. My motto: “Nature knows best.”

name: Priscille CAZIN
bio: As a compost facilitator Priscille supports organizations and individuals in understanding/making quality compost. She designs workshops & training programs (FR, IT) to share accessible practical know-how. Four years ago she shifted her focus to microbiology and soil life deepening her experience thanks to Soil Food Web techniques. Her lab assesses composts’ and soils’ biological vitality. Her aim is to help growers, landowners, municipalities, etc. in Belgium, France and Italy to manage their own microbe rich composts (+extracts & teas) that can enhance/restore their soils’ and crops’ health

name: Quinn Turner
bio: Avid soil biology advocate, with a background in mechanical engineering, and potato automation. Passionate about growing fruit trees in the high mountain desert of Idaho.

name: Rebecca Iannicelli
bio: My focus is on soil regeneration in a suburban setting to promote hyper-local food production.

name: Renald Flores
bio: Florès Sens System, led by CEO Renald Flores, has spent the past five years traveling globally to identify leading practices in soil microbiology, regenerative agriculture and grazing, agroecology, permaculture design, and holistic decision-making.rnrnThey now deliver integrated solutions in soil ecosystem regeneration, microbiological analysis, BioComplete™ compost production (training and multi-scale setup), regenerative farm design (grazing, crops, cover crops, no-till), and transition management toward fully organic, soil-regenerating systems.

name: Robbin Pott
bio: Robbin Pott co-founded Pott Farms, L3C, a Regenerative Organic Certified educational hemp farm offering internships for young adults affected by poverty and trauma. Formerly a law and public policy professional in child welfare at the University of Michigan, she shifted to farming in 2016 to help youth build stability and skills. To support the farm’s mission, Robbin offers Living Soil Services, providing soil testing, consulting, education, and compost products.

name: Robert
bio: Inoculated with the passion for soil health starting at an early age on a family orchard in Europe. My interests have grown to include the understanding of human health a soil health connection. The focus of my +7 years have been the production of BCC compost, biochar and related products on a commercial scale.

name: Ronald Cain
bio: Ronald studied horticulture in college and following graduation in 2015 he found Dr. Elaine’s™ Soil Food Web courses. In these courses he learned exactly how to utilize a microscope and make high quality compost, teas, and extracts. With the knowledge and experience Ronald has gained, he focuses on helping others to rebuild soil health, manage ecology and restore land.

name: Rosa Pertierra Lazo
bio: I am an agronomist (Chile) with a PhD in Agricultural Sciences (Germany). I graduated from the SFW program in 2021 and have since managed my consulting and laboratory analysis services independently. To date, I have worked with the SFW methodology on walnut and hazelnut orchards, vineyards, vegetables, and pastures.

name: Saoirse Niehus
bio: Saoirse started her biological soil testing laboratory in 2026 at the young age of 17. Having spent her childhood growing up on first a 30-acre farm and later a property designed on permaculture principles, she founded Gaea Regenerative Land Care based on a desire to show others the amazing truth about the soil and nature as a whole. She has been homeschooled her entire life and chose to enroll in Dr. Elaine’s SFW School rather than going to college; she has already achieved her Lab-Tech certification and is currently enrolled in the Consultant Training Program.

name: Sarah Sobel
bio: Je m\’engage à faire de la santé des sols une priorité pour les jardiniers et les agriculteurs. Je partagerai mes connaissances avec ceux qui recherchent en les guidant dans la création de composts Biocomplete, d\’extraits, ainsi que dans l\’identification microbienne grâce à l\’analyse biologique des sols. rnrnI am committed to bringing soil health as a primary topic for gardeners/farmers of all sizes. I will share my knowledge to those in search of regenerative practices through guidance in creating Biocomplete composts, extracts, teas and microbial identification with soil health analysis.

name: Sarah Talia
bio: At Living Microbes, I specialize in providing biological analysis of soil and compost to help clients achieve optimal agricultural productivity. I offer a wide range of services, including microbial identification and soil health assessments.

name: Scott Kent
bio: Hungry Worms is one of the largest red wiggler suppliers in the USA. I also specialize in analyzing worm casting microbiology using soil food web methodology.

name: Scott Walker
bio: I’m an organic lawn and soil practitioner based in central North Carolina and founder of Pleasant Green Grass. For over two decades, I’ve focused on improving soil health in compacted, clay dominant Piedmont soils. My work centers on building organic matter, improving structure, and restoring biological function in real world conditions where topsoil is stripped and irrigation is limited. Through my involvement with the Soil Food Web community, I aim to connect soil biology principles with practical land care that creates healthier, more resilient landscapes.

name: Sedrika \Maka\” Anuhealii”””
bio: Born and raised in the islands since the early 1970ʻs, Sedrika had observed the turn of plantation land change from productive commodity to barren fields due to soil degradation and mismanagement. She desired to become a part of the solution to regenerate the health of the soil and find ways to increase the island\’s access to its own food sources. After certifying as a Certified Lab Tech with the Soil Food Web School, she now works full-time in soil science-related fields and is working towards completion of the Consultant Training Program.

name: Seshu
bio: Deeply committed to growing vegetables and fruits that are rich in nutrients. He has a six acre farm in Mysore, India where in he grows fruits and vegetables using regenerate principles and Soil Food Web science. With his knowledge and experience, he intends to convert neighbouring farmers from chemical to natural farming.

name: Shane Plath
bio: Shane is a passionate horticulturalist with 20 years of organic farming experience. Together with his family, he runs South Africa’s largest organic banana farm—over 1,800 hectares employing more than 2,000 workers.rnrnIn 2015, the farm faced rising costs, heat stress, pests, disease, and declining yields despite long-standing EU organic certification. After studying Dr. Elaine’s™ work and online courses, Shane shifted to a biological approach, producing and applying large volumes of BioComplete™ Compost and Compost Tea.

name: Simeon Kleinsasser
bio: Simeon Kleinsasser is a soil scientist with an engineering background who helps farmers, ranchers, and land managers transition to regenerative practices based on the six principles of regenerative agriculture. His work focuses on on-farm fertility systems that reduce reliance on external inputs. Drawing from experience in plant science and engineering, Simeon has contributed to the development of the Hiwassee Products line of equipment tailored to support producers in building biologically resilient, healthy soils.

name: Sofya Brown
bio: Sofya’s expertise stems from formal studies in environmental engineering, a certification in permaculture design, and specialized training with the Soil Food Web School. She focuses on soil microbiome function and regenerative agronomy, applying Albrecht’s mineral balancing method to enhance soil fertility. Her science-based, holistic approach supports vibrant ecosystems for regenerative agriculture and ecological landscaping.

name: Soledad Reinoso
bio: I am an Organic Crop Production Technician, Soil Food Web–Certified Microscopist, and specialist in Regenerative Agriculture and Holistic Livestock Management. At LaEnmienda, we guide producers across Argentina in transitioning to regenerative/organic systems. We prioritize soil health with science-based practices and monitoring tools to track real progress. We partner with farms of all sizes nationwide, regenerating soil, economic viability, and social well-being. First SoilFoodWeb–Certified Lab in the Spanish-speaking world (2023) +1,000 soil/compost analyses. Specialized courses&trainings.
area: VICENTE LOPEZ - FLORIDA OESTE, BUENOS AIRES, Argentina

name: Sonja Basson – Pure Soil Lab
bio: I have a passion for connection, connecting all life, macro and micro. Mostly interested in the relationships we don\’t understand yet. I am a soil nerd, enjoy every single minute that I get to spend with soil and microbes. I am a CTP student at Dr Elaine\’s SFW School and I have been growing fruit, veg and herbs for the last 13 years. Currently I am putting all my knowledge that I get from the CTP program in growing nutrient dense fruit and vegetables.

name: Spero Latchis
bio: For nine years Spero Latchis, CCH. operated a free homeopathic clinic in rural Himalayan India. He understands that the health of all living beings, is inseparably connected with the biological health of our soils. In 2017 he moved to Maine and founded the nonprofit Living Soil Network. He currently consults on agricultural and landscaping projects. Spero manages Living Soil Farm in Palermo, Maine using only beneficial microbes and agro homeopathy. He is a NOFA certified landscape consultant. Through the Living Soil Company he offers 30 yards of living compost for sale each year.

name: Stephanie McDaniel
bio: Test Bio

name: Stephen Suau
bio: Stephen Suau is a SFW certified lab technician and professional engineer with 40 years of experience in watershed management and restoration serving government agencies as well as large property owners and agriculturalists. Mr. Suau has a Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Illinois in Civil Engineering. Mr. Suau has been recognized with numerous awards including 2022 Certificate of Commendation for outstanding achievement in over 35 years of water quality solutions of the City and County of Sarasota, Florida from the Sarasota Soil and Water Conservation District.

name: Steven Fleming
bio: I am a small farmer in SE Scotland dabbling in regenerative agriculture. I have completed the Soil Food Web Technician Course and can examine soil and compost samples microscopically to assess their biological content.

name: Stine Hvidtfeldt Svendsen
bio: I’m the founder of Hållbar Jord & Växt SWE AB, a sustainable garden and soil service based in Malmö, Sweden, near Copenhagen.rnI am a certified lab-tech., and I combine practical garden care with scientific knowledge of soil health. I collect garden waste, turn it into nutrient-rich compost, and cultivate beneficial microbes that I return to my customers — helping gardens grow stronger in a natural and sustainable way.nI also provide soil and compost analysis for private clients and companies. If you need help with your garden, soil or compost, please get in touch.

name: Sue Patrick
bio: Self-confessed soil biology nerd. Small scale vermicomposter. Avid regenerative fan.

name: SURINDER SARWARA
bio: My family background is with farming by generations and I am not able to figure out why farmers who feeds the whole world can barely makes a living ,besides lots of reasons the one that stuck me the most is why the cost of production is going higher while quality of production is decreasing and leading to many diseases with humans and there animals in general. This search led me to Soil Food Web and I am so happy for all the educational and general awareness created by school around the world , I am glad to be part of this Nobel cause.

name: Sustraiak Koop.
bio: Sustraiak Habitat Design, a Cooperative dedicated to promoting the agroecological transition using Regenerative Agriculture tools and from a Social and Solidarity Economy perspective. Since 2016, we have developed over 120 projects, worked with more than 300 farmers, delivered over 200 training sessions, and facilitated the regeneration of more than 4,000 hectares.

name: Suzanne Shea
bio: Certified Soil Food Web Lab Technician and Certified Soil Food Web Consultant based in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. Suzanne provides microscope-based soil testing and practical guidance to help farmers, gardeners, schools, and land managers understand the living biology in their soil. She works with native, biologically complete compost and compost extracts and helps clients match soil biology to the crops they want to grow.

name: Tallis Tibbo
bio: I bring 20+ years’ experience designing and managing food security projects across Africa for the United Nations and UK Government. I’ve managed complex large-scale projects building evidence around solutions for drought-affected farmers in East & Southern Africa. Now training to become a Soil Food Web Consultant, my interest is in trialling commercially viable soil health strategies that strengthen profitability and resilience, particularly in grassland and livestock systems.

name: Tanja Dekker
bio: Tanja has years of experience in soil restoration. She provides expert advice on soil improvement plans and offers hands-on support for their implementation. Tanja is also affiliated with the Botanical Garden of TU Delft. She leverages her knowledge and experience to help farmers transition from a chemical-based approach to a biological one, using the SFW-approa
area: The Hague, South Holland, Netherlands Antilles

name: Thomas Rüttel
bio: Based in Hoofddorp, The Netherlands, I work with clients throughout the country. I specialize in microscopic analysis of soil, compost, compost extracts, and compost teas. On request, on-site sampling and additional crop measurements can be included.rnrnWorking with crop advisors, farmers, and professionals in green management and sports fields, I provide soil biology data to improve soil function and plant performance. I also have experience in project-based work in collaboration with SFW Consultants.

name: Thomas Schneider
bio: Thomas Schneider has spent nearly his whole life working in Regenerative Agriculture and Landscape Design. After training with Dr. Ingham, In 2015 Thomas started DynamicWholeScapes, a company which focuses on regenerative agriculture education, consultations, and projects.

name: Tim Spencer
bio: I started my avocado growing career in 2022 purchasing a small orchard. After learning the industrial system and navigating the export requirements, I soon looked for a more profitable system with less external inputs. I completed the SFW FC and moved on to the GTP and microscopy programs and quickly put my learnings into practice developing composting, extraction and application methods at a suitable scale for the size of the property. I have now been transitioning into agroecological farming practices since late 2024. Happy to share learnings and FAILs-First Attempt In Learning!
area: Ōmokoroa, Bay of Plenty, New Zealand

name: Todd Harrington
bio: Todd has spent his life dedicated to the field of biological regenerative soil restoration. Building on the work of Dr. Elaine Ingham, Todd has pioneered methods and systems of restoring land and agriculture fertility. His methods are tested in the real world, on working farms, nurseries, greenhouses, vineyards, orchards, turf fields and landscapes. Clients who work with Todd and his team often gain far more than just results, they gain a permanent relationship and the confidence to achieve their vision for their land.

name: Vera Dorzhinova
bio: Vera is a former software engineer currently developing a career in soil health. In 2020 she found out about permaculture, regenerative ag and soil microbes and absolutely fell in love with the soil-ution to almost all the world’s problems. Same year she enrolled in the Soil Food Web School classes to learn soil microscopy and how to make soil-healing amendments like biologically rich compost, extracts, and teas. Vera is a certified Soil Food Web Consultant and Lab-Tech at Veriterra Lab that was created to support farmers, gardeners, and landscapers in implementing soil regenerative practices.

name: Veronica Alice
bio: Builder & tender of soil Microbial habitats, for extract & breeding purposes. Clients range from the Sunshine Coast Community Forest to the backyard gardeners.
area: Area D (Roberts Creek), British Columbia, Canada

name: Vivian Kaloxilos
bio: DocTerre was founded in 2015 by Vivian Kaloxilos, graduate of McGill University School of Environment with ecological field experience at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute. She was the first Canadian to complete the full certification training with Dr. Ingham in 2015, after several years of practical demonstrations, ecological field work, agro-ecological design, and agricultural experience.

name: Wendy Mickle
bio: Wendy is a certified Soil Food Web Consultant and founder of MicrobeGrower, where she helps growers and farmers put soil biology to work in practical, meaningful ways. An experienced educator who has taught all ages and levels, Wendy has a gift for making complex biological concepts easy to understand and apply. She offers hands-on training and online classes alongside precision tools and custom inoculants to help clients build biologically resilient soils that perform season after season.

name: Wesley Sander
bio: Wesley Sander has spent most of his life in and around agriculture. He grew up raising farm animals on a small acreage, then studied journalism and environmental biology before spending the next decade covering farm-related topics for several publications. After that came a transition to small-farm management, and the discovery of just what can be accomplished when the soil foodweb is put to proper use. This all culminated in FoothillBio, established in 2015 to help clients understand their soils’ living communities through laboratory analysis and consultation.

name: Wesley Soule
bio: We offer a range of microbial and chemical testing services to the Wine region of the Western Cape of South Africa. We work extensively in viticulture but have worked across a range of crops in South Africa, orchards, grain, and pasture systems. Our work has taken us into waste management and compost operation development for a number of producers. Our lab is at a Biogas facility where we provide analysis for their team. We have worked in carbon development projects, germination/growth trials and the production of biofertilisers. Feel free to reach out to learn more about our work.
area: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

name: Witold Krawiec
bio: I am fascinated by the microbial life beneath our feet. As a Certified Soil Lab-Tech based in Toronto, Ontario, I support gardeners and small-scale farmers through soil assessments, identifying imbalances in nutrient-cycling microorganisms within the soil food web. Through my affiliation with Toronto Compost, I collaborate with a dedicated community committed to soil education, building healthy composts, and promoting regenerative ecosystems. I envision biologically active soils everywhere, where nutrient-dense food cultivation strengthens the health of people, animals, and our planet.
